beats.text: It was not one box of 90,000 cards.
beats.note: The figure is real, but Bielefeld University describes two largely separate collections: about 23,000 cards in the first and about 67,000 in the second.

beats.text: Every card had a fixed address.
beats.note: Card 1,1 was followed by 1,2. A later insertion became 1,1a, then 1,1a1. The archive reports codes of up to 13 characters.
The archive notes that the entries are undated, even though the cards were written between 1951 and 1996.

beats.context: about how many notes the Luhmann Archive counts across both collections.

beats.note: The archive credits Niklas Luhmann with approaching 600 publications, including more than 40 monographs.

beats.text: Ninety thousand notes, and every one had an address.
